collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager's daily predictions keep coming true and a gift seems possible: ask for a harder one, or try to make one fail.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has started making a prediction every morning. "Today, someone will laugh." "Today, the sun will set." "Today, (friend) will eat a fish." Every single one has come true. (subject) is beginning to think (subject.he/she) might have a gift.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) asks for a prediction about something that might not happen. (subject) closes (subject.his/her) eyes, thinks, and says, "Tomorrow it will rain on the far side of the island." Nobody goes to check. (subject) counts it as a success. (friend) isn't entirely sure (friend.he/she) can argue with that.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) refuses to eat any fish all day, on principle. By evening (friend.he/she) is very hungry. (subject) points out that the prediction never said which day. (friend) eats a fish. (subject) declares a triumph.
